subject.title: fix: resolve Codex fork duplication when parent is unresolved (#2108)

question: Which branch should become the canonical Codex fork-accounting implementation after this PR’s two current-head defects are repaired?
rationale: Both open PRs modify intersecting session identity, parent dependency, and cache ownership rules; automated review cannot safely choose the permanent compatibility contract or authorize two competing implementations.

options.title: Consolidate into proven branch
options.body: Use https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2118 as the canonical branch and port only this PR’s validated provenance-backed row logic after repairing its defects.

options.title: Consolidate into this PR
options.body: Repair this branch, add equivalent frozen-corpus cold/warm proof, and absorb the overlapping session-identity and parent-fingerprint behavior here.

options.title: Pause both branches
options.body: Hold both implementations until maintainers agree on a narrower family-ledger contract against the real corpus.

recommendation.title: Consolidate into proven branch
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2118 as the canonical branch and port only this PR’s validated provenance-backed row logic after repairing its defects.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository owner is the best available authority to choose the permanent parser/cache contract and canonical landing branch.
